content: 1. Sarecycline and Posaconazole: Posaconazole levels or effects are increased by sarecycline through inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely for toxicities and consider dosage adjustments if necessary. 2. Posaconazole and Saxagliptin: Posaconazole increases saxagliptin levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required, and therapy adjustments may be necessary, especially when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 3. Posaconazole and Seladelpar: Posaconazole increases seladelpar levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers and are also taking moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 4. Selpercatinib and Posaconazole: Co-administration increases the risk of QTc prolongation. Avoid this combination or use an alternative therapy. 5. Selumetinib and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases selumetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or reduce the selumetinib dose if unavoidable. Resume the original selumetinib dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives. 6. Sertraline and Posaconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Sevoflurane and Posaconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 8. Sildenafil and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases sildenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Silodosin and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases silodosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 10. Simvastatin and Posaconazole: Posaconazole significantly increases simvastatin levels, leading to an increased risk of rhabdomyolysis. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Siponimod and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases siponimod levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. Both drugs also increase the QTc interval. 12. Sirolimus and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 13. Sodium Bicarbonate and Posaconazole: Sodium bicarbonate decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Sodium Citrate/Citric Acid and Posaconazole: Similar to sodium bicarbonate, this combination decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Sodium Sulfate/Potassium Chloride/Magnesium Sulfate/Polyethylene Glycol and Posaconazole: Both agents decrease serum potassium levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 16. Sodium Zirconium Cyclosilicate and Posaconazole: This combination decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. Monitor closely. 17. Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases the levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Solifenacin and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases solifenacin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. Both drugs also increase the QTc interval. 19. Sonidegib and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases sonidegib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 20. Sorafenib and Posaconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 21. Sotalol and Posaconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 22. Sotorasib and Posaconazole: Sotorasib decreases posaconazole levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or refer to prescribing information for dosage modifications if unavoidable. 23. Sparsentan and Posaconazole: Co-administration increases toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid this combination or interrupt sparsentan treatment if unavoidable. 24. St. John’s Wort and Posaconazole: St. John’s Wort decreases posaconazole levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Stiripentol and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases stiripentol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 26. Streptomycin and Posaconazole: Posaconazole decreases streptomycin levels through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unclear. 27. Sufentanil and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases sufentanil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. 28. Sulfamethoxazole and Posaconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Sunitinib and Posaconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 30. Suvorexant and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases suvorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 31. Tacrolimus and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases tacrolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. Both drugs also increase the QTc interval. 32. Tadalafil and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases tadalafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Talazoparib and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases talazoparib levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely. 34. Tamoxifen and Posaconazole: Posaconazole inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing the conversion of tamoxifen to its active metabolite. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Tamsulosin and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases tamsulosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 36. Tasimetleon and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases tasimetleon levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Tazemetostat and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases tazemetostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 38. Telavancin and Posaconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Temsirolimus and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases temsirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Teniposide and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases teniposide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 41. Tepotinib and Posaconazole: Tepotinib increases posaconazole levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or reduce the P-gp substrate dosage if unavoidable. 42. Terbinafine and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases terbinafine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Tetrabenazine and Posaconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 44. Tezacaftor and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases tezacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 45. Theophylline and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases theophylline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Thioridazine and Posaconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Tiagabine and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases tiagabine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 48. Ticagrelor and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases ticagrelor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 49. Tinidazole and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases tinidazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Tipranavir and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Tisotumab Vedotin and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases tisotumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 52. Tobramycin and Posaconazole: Posaconazole decreases tobramycin levels through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unclear. 53. Tofacitinib and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases tofacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg daily. 54. Tolterodine and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases tolterodine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Tolvaptan and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases tolvaptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 56. Toremifene and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases toremifene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Trabectedin and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases trabectedin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 58. Tramadol and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases tramadol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 59. Trazodone and Posaconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 60. Triamcinolone Acetonide Injectable Suspension and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases triamcinolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Triazolam and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases triazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Trifluoperazine and Posaconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 63. Trimethoprim and Posaconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Trimipramine and Posaconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 65. Tropisetron and Posaconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Tucatinib and Posaconazole: Tucatinib increases posaconazole levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates. 67. Ubrogepant and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases ubrogepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy.
